newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SUPERBIKE-FOGARTY LOSES FLEETING LEAD TO KOCINSKI.
newsitem.headline: SUPERBIKE-FOGARTY LOSES FLEETING LEAD TO KOCINSKI.

text.p: Briton Carl Fogarty tasted glory and defeat at the Austrian superbike world championship event on Sunday, winning his first race and then colliding in his second to relinquish his short-lived overall lead.

The Ducati rider topped the podium after the first of two races at the A1-Ring. He was .297 seconds ahead of Japan's Akiro Yanagawa on a Kawasaki and .615 clear of New Zealand's Aaron Slight on a Honda.
In the first race five riders were within a second of each other nearing the line until Fogarty broke away and won in 38 minutes 11.804 seconds after 25 laps.
But in the second race, Fogarty caused a crash with his fiercest rival, Honda rider John Kocinski, when he tried to overtake the American.
Kocinski had just taken the lead from Fogarty when both men slid off-track. The Briton was forced to abandon but Kocinski was able to remount his bike and continue.
The American recovered sensationally to finish third and regain the overall lead in the standings with 273 points to Fogarty's 267 points and Slight's 223.
The crash between the sport's two leading men allowed Yanagawa to become the first Japanese rider to win a superbike world championship race outside his home country.
A delighted Yanagawa crossed the finish line 0.121 seconds ahead of Slight and 7.264 ahead of Kocinski.
